title: Long Context Falloff Compendium data file

lines.description: Serving lines: one rig, one engine, one set of weights and flags, and the points measured on it. Named-model results live here; platforms[].perf stays the older proxy-model layer and the two are not mixed in any chart.

candidates.description: Rigs under consideration that have no measured line yet. Cost, capacity and bandwidth are derived from their units, so a candidate cannot disagree with the catalog.

key_findings.description: Prose synthesis of the appendix sections above. Not itself a source of numbers — every figure it restates must already be sourced in its section.

appendixSection.description: A secondary dataset merged in from an unmerged branch rather than modeled as units/platforms/builds — e.g. an anecdotal architecture comparison or a one-off lab benchmark. Loosely typed on purpose (shapes vary), but every section must say where it came from, and every individual number in it must carry a confidence code the same as any other measurement on this page.

confidence.description: m = measured primary · m~ = measured secondary/anecdotal · e = extrapolated · i = modeled from specs. Absence means no data; there is no code for it.

measurement.description: A benchmark number and how much to trust it. Tuple form for the common case, object form when it needs provenance.

contexts.description: The shared prefill x-axis. Adding a point here makes a column appear everywhere; platforms without that key render as gaps.

confidence.description: Human-readable gloss for each confidence code, rendered in the legend.

asOf.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM. A price without a date is not a fact.

pricing.description: Open by design: add lease/used/bundle alongside msrp and street without a schema change.

power.description: Draw for ONE unit, observed under LLM inference. Deliberately not hardware.tdpW: inference is bandwidth-bound and does not reach the datasheet ceiling, and cards are commonly power-capped. Build totals are summed from this, never stored.

unit.description: A quantity of one platform or one catalog unit. Exactly one of `platform` or `unit` must be given.

unsupported.description: True when this platform provably cannot run the archetype (capacity, not missing data). The note should say why.

prefill.description: Prefill throughput keyed by exact prompt length in tokens. Keying by token count rather than array position means a value can never drift away from its confidence code, and an absent context is a gap rather than a silent shift.

perf.description: Keyed by archetype id from meta.archetypes. Absent archetypes render as em dashes.

extra.description: Escape hatch for data captured before anyone decided how to render it. Nothing reads this.

build.description: A purchasable box, expressed as the units it contains. Cost and power are summed from those units and never stored here.

host.description: Whatever the units do not account for: chassis, CPU, PSU, cooling. Keeps the residual visible instead of hidden inside a card price.

catalogUnit.description: A purchasable piece of hardware -- the thing a datasheet describes. Platforms and builds are quantities of these, so a price or spec corrected here corrects everything containing it.

tdpW.description: Datasheet TDP. Recorded only; nothing derives from it -- see power.

values.description: Rated throughput keyed by precision (fp32, tf32, bf16, fp16, fp8, fp4, int8, ...). Suffix a key with ':sparse' for structured-sparsity figures. New precisions need no schema change.

unknown.description: Precisions believed supported (or at least not ruled out) that no sourced figure was found for after a real search -- rendered as a colored '?' rather than a blank dash, so 'we don't have a number yet' reads differently from 'confirmed unsupported' or 'never looked'. Not a dumping ground for every unresearched precision -- only add a key here after an actual search came up empty.

unsupported.description: Precisions confirmed architecturally absent on this part (not merely undocumented) -- still rendered as a dash, kept separate from 'unknown' so the two are never conflated. The reasoning belongs in the unit's note, not duplicated here.

sources.description: Where this record's specifications came from. Required once any specification field is filled, so an unsourced number cannot land quietly.

note.description: Caveats — e.g. that a bandwidth figure is SoC-wide rather than a discrete card's.

composition.description: What this configuration is made of. Cost, power and capacity are summed from it; storing them directly is not allowed.

rig.description: The hardware a line ran on, or a candidate would run on: catalog units, how they are connected, and the host around them. Cost, power draw and capacity are derived from the units and never stored here.

interconnect.description: How the units talk to each other. Absent means nobody has looked; say so in a note rather than guessing a link type.

kind.description: nvlink, infinity-fabric, xe-link, pcie ... free text on purpose, so a new fabric needs no schema change.

p2p.description: Whether peer-to-peer transfers were actually enabled for the run. A container or VM can disable them without anyone noticing.

powerCapW.description: Per-unit power cap the run was under, if any.

provenance.description: Where a number came from and how far to trust the route it took. `kind` says what sort of source it is; `authorship` says who produced it. Authorship is declared, never inferred: a measurement is weighed by whether its inputs can be checked, not by who typed it.

source.description: A repository path, issue or comment reference, or URL -- enough to go and read the original.

digest.description: sha256 of the manifest that pins the receipts, when one exists.

reproduced.description: Whether anyone other than the reporter has reproduced the numbers. Required for issue-report and forum sources.

linePoint.description: One number from one line. Depth, stream count and per-stream-versus-aggregate are always stated, because a bare tok/s means three different things without them.

depth.description: Context tokens already in the session, per stream, when the point was taken.

basis.description: One stream is always per-stream; aggregate means the total across streams.

range.description: Low and high across repeated runs, when the source reports a range rather than one figure. Give exactly one of value or range.

spec.description: Whether speculative decoding was active for this point, when it differs from the line's default.

prefillBasis.description: Prefill only. cold = the whole prompt was evaluated; new-tokens = the rate over only the tokens not already cached.

acceptance.description: Draft acceptance, as the engine defines it. Not comparable across engines.

line.description: One serving line. Every result belongs to exactly one, so engine, quant, cache type and speculation are never implied by a table row.

lineage.description: upstream, fork, vendor ... where the code comes from and who maintains it. Free text: specialist engines exist for most of this hardware.

kld.description: KL divergence of the quantized model against a stated reference, on code and on prose. Quality, not speed: tok/s across different quants is not the same product.

kibPerToken.description: Measured KV cost per token on this engine. The config-derived figure is a lower bound on it (see tools/test-kv.mjs).

tokens.description: The KV pool as loaded. Under a unified pool this is shared by every slot, not a per-request limit.

registryId.description: The Discipline substrate id, when the line is one.

admission.description: Discipline's own word, only where a registry entry carries one. Absent for lines that are characterization only.

status.description: withdrawn = the build or configuration is known to produce invalid numbers; say why in hazards.

candidate.description: A rig under consideration with no measured line yet.
